one_liner: Unreleased AVX-512 ML-KEM (ESORICS 2024) reporting 1.30-1.64x fewer cycles than pq-crystals AVX2 Kyber, but only 0.4-5.6% more TLS handshakes.
what_it_does: An ESORICS 2024 paper from Fudan University describing an AVX-512 implementation of ML-KEM-512/768/1024. It is built on the pq-crystals Kyber 'standard' branch (FIPS 203 draft code) and passes NIST KATs. The authors added it to liboqs 0.10.1 as extra ML-KEM Keygen/Encaps/Decaps functions behind an OQS config macro, then ran TLS 1.3 handshakes through the OQS provider on OpenSSL 3.3.0-dev. The paper also proposes an 8-key batch keygen and benchmarks non-FIPS IND-1-CCA variants (TCH, TRH) that skip re-encryption. None of the code has been released.
how_it_is_fast: Each 512-bit zmm register holds 32 signed 16-bit coefficients, so one polynomial fits in 8 registers. All 7 NTT layers are merged: coefficients load once, and shuffle16/8/4/2/1 permutes pair them up at each butterfly distance. The butterflies use signed Montgomery reduction (vpmullw/vpmulhw with twiddles premultiplied by q^-1), Barrett reduction (vpmulhw plus a shift), and lazy reduction in the inverse NTT. Keccak-p[1600] runs 8 states in parallel instead of AVX2's 4. Rejection sampling and CBD sampling use AVX-512 mask registers and compress-store, and pk/sk decode and decompress use the byte permute vpermb.
when_to_use: As a design blueprint if you maintain an ML-KEM backend for AVX-512 x86 servers such as Sapphire Rapids and want roughly 1.3-1.6x over the pq-crystals AVX2 kernels.
TLS terminators or KEM key pools that can pre-generate ephemeral keys 8 at a time: batched keygen is reported at 2,804 / 4,866 / 7,394 cycles per key for ML-KEM-512/768/1024.
Capacity planning: the paper's handshake data shows faster KEM code barely moves openssl s_time throughput, which is useful evidence before spending effort on KEM kernels.
Research on IND-1-CCA KEMs for ephemeral TLS key exchange: TRH decaps is 5,666 vs 19,838 cycles for ML-KEM-512 (measured on the AVX2 code), with the same ciphertext size.
when_not_to_use: When you need something you can build or audit: the paper says 'we will later open source our code', and no repository was found as of 2026-09. The only public AVX-512 Kyber repo found (cccccosine/Kyber_AVX512_32w) is a different ISC 2024 multi-way paper.
CPUs without AVX-512: the design depends on 32 zmm registers, mask registers, compress-store and vpermb, and has no fallback path.
Hybrid-mode TLS (X25519/P-256 + ML-KEM) where you expect big handshake gains: Table 4 shows about 0.4-5.6% more connections/sec, because ECDH and signatures dominate.

Deployments that need final-FIPS 203 or CMVP conformance: the code was built on FIPS 203 draft base code, final-standard conformance is not documented, and the faster TRH/TCH variants are not ML-KEM at all.
One-off keygen latency: batching only pays off when the caller consumes 8 key pairs at once, which needs application or protocol changes.

integration.form: not applicable: paper only. It describes a source patch to liboqs 0.10.1 (ml_kem directory) used via oqs-provider, and it was never released.
integration.dependencies: not documented (unreleased); the paper's integration used liboqs 0.10.1, oqs-provider and OpenSSL 3.3.0-dev
integration.min_toolchain: GCC 9.4.0 in the paper's evaluation, optimization flags not stated; kernels are shown as GNU-as AT&T-syntax macros
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX-512 (including the vpermb byte permute), evaluated only on a 4-vCPU Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8i.xlarge (Xeon Platinum 8475B, Sapphire Rapids)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: per the paper it slots into liboqs as alternate ML-KEM Keygen/Encaps/Decaps behind an OQS_ENABLE_KEM_ml_kem_512_avx512 config macro, so OQS-provider and OpenSSL callers do not change. But the code is unreleased, and batch keygen requires callers to take 8 keys at a time.

gotchas: Table 3 anomaly: the AVX2 ML-KEM-1024/Dilithium5 cell (3191.46 conn/s) duplicates the Falcon512 cell, so AVX-512 appears slower there (2451.08). It also contradicts the paper's own statement that handshakes/sec drop as the security level rises, so it is likely a copy error and that column is unreliable.

The batch-keygen ratios printed in Table 2 (4.9x/4.2x/3.5x) are a bit higher than the same table's non-batched AVX-512 keygen implies (about 4.7x/4.0x/3.4x). Also, Algorithm 4 as printed batches only the final SHA3-256 over the 8 encapsulation keys while K-PKE.KeyGen runs in a loop, so the paper does not explain how per-key cost falls to 2,804 cycles.

The printed assembly has errors: Algorithm 2 (Gentleman-Sande butterfly) repeats 'vpmulhw %zmm\zh' on two lines where a low-half product with the zeta*q^-1 constant is needed, so do not transcribe the listings verbatim.

Noisy measurement setup: Turbo Boost and hyper-threading were left on, the host was a 4-vCPU cloud VM, and TLS client and server ran on the same machine. Handshake deltas of about 1-5% are within what such setups can drift.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: It is the only catalogued AVX-512 ML-KEM result, so use it as a reference design; for runnable ML-KEM code, moduletto (NEON ML-KEM-512 on aarch64, benchmarked against liboqs 0.16.0) actually ships. The same group's Dilithium-AVX512 (the paper's ref [56]) has public code for the signature side, and ENG25519 (ref [55]) speeds up the X25519 half that this paper's own data shows dominates hybrid handshakes.
verified_claims_summary: On a 4-vCPU Alibaba c8i VM (Xeon Platinum 8475B, GCC 9.4.0, flags unstated, Turbo and HT on), the median over 100,000 runs shows the AVX-512 code using 1.30-1.64x fewer cycles than the pq-crystals 'standard'-branch AVX2 Kyber built with AVX-512 disabled (for example, ML-KEM-1024 encaps at 25,062 vs 41,162 cycles). Through liboqs 0.10.1, the OQS provider and OpenSSL 3.3.0-dev, openssl s_time handshakes/sec rose only about 0.4-5.6% in PQ-only and hybrid modes.
status_note: Peer-reviewed (ESORICS 2024, LNCS pp. 123-143), but the promised code never appeared, liboqs has no AVX-512 ML-KEM from this work (it switched to mlkem-native in 2025), and there is no license or maintenance, so treat it as a paper-only reference design.
